findings.title: Reclaim abandoned partial backups to preserve the disk bound
findings.trigger: The process is killed during a retry backup copy, or after copying but before renaming, and subsequently restarts. Repeated interruptions leave distinct timestamped .partial files.
findings.execution_path: create_lifespan → init_db → run_migrations writes a timestamp-specific .partial file. SIGKILL bypasses the exception cleanup. The next startup chooses a new timestamp, while _prune_timestamped_backups rejects every old .partial suffix.
findings.consequence: Abandoned copies accumulate without limit and can fill the data volume, preventing startup despite the advertised bounded upgrade backups.
findings.evidence: Cleanup only targets the current attempt's partial_path inside the exception handler. Lines 208–210 exclude abandoned partials from retention. test_failed_retry_backup_copy_leaves_no_candidate_and_spares_good_backups explicitly seeds a hard-kill leftover but only checks the count of completed backups; it does not assert reclamation or bound total backup storage.
findings.suggested_fix: Add safe reclamation or bounded reuse of abandoned staging files, with ownership/locking sufficient to avoid deleting an active concurrent copy. Keep incomplete files excluded from the three valid recovery backups. Add a restart regression that seeds multiple abandoned partials and checks their reclamation alongside preservation of valid backups.
findings.hypothesis: Repeated hard termination during the copy/rename window leaves one additional unprunable partial per attempt. This follows from the inspected control flow; an actual process-kill reproduction was not run.
